name: registry.value.create
description: Create a new registry value. Errors with `already_exists` if the value is already present; use `registry.value.update` to overwrite. Creates the parent key if missing.

path.description: Registry key path in `HKLM\Software\...` form. Created if missing.

value.description: Value name. Empty string for the (Default) value.

data.description: Value data, formatted per `type`. REG_SZ/REG_EXPAND_SZ/REG_LINK: the literal string. REG_DWORD/REG_QWORD: decimal-stringified integer (or `0xHEX`). REG_BINARY: base64. REG_MULTI_SZ: lines separated by `\n` (agent converts to null-separated).

x-output-schema.description: Empty body — wire response is the literal `OK 0`.

x-implementations.name: reg_create_set_new
x-implementations.description: Win32 `RegCreateKeyExW` (creates parent key if missing; opens with KEY_QUERY_VALUE | KEY_SET_VALUE) + `RegQueryValueExW` (probe to detect existing value) + `RegSetValueExW`. Returns ERR already_exists when the probe finds the value present.

windows-modern.description: RegCreateKeyExW + probe + RegSetValueExW. The probe step makes create vs. update explicit at this layer (Win32 RegSetValueExW itself doesn't distinguish). HKLM writes typically require admin; ERR permission_denied without elevation.

windows-classic.description: Same APIs since NT 3.1. NT 4 / 9x agents use RegSetValueExA with ANSI transcoding for string types. Win 9x lacks REG_QWORD and REG_LINK — those return ERR not_supported.
